narrative:
The model estimates a 62% chance that you will leave your current role, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

The strongest influence is that you have received other job opportunities while at your current employer. Having external offers is a major signal the model associates with a higher likelihood of leaving, and this factor pushed the prediction most strongly toward departure.

Your six to ten years of experience in this organization worked in the opposite direction. Employees predicted to stay tend to have shorter tenures here, so your relatively long time in this role slightly pulled the prediction back toward staying. Similarly, your overall career experience of six to ten years also nudged the outcome slightly toward staying, though this effect was weaker than the impact of external opportunities.

Taken together, the presence of outside offers outweighed the stabilizing effect of your tenure, leading to the decision against promotion. You and your manager should discuss what would make staying more attractive, whether through clearer advancement paths, better recognition of your experience, or addressing whatever is drawing you toward other opportunities. Understanding these drivers now gives you a chance to influence the outcome before any decision becomes final.
